answer: The nonce chain allows at most 4 challenge submissions per identity per epoch, which means extra aliases are the only way to submit more. Each extra alias then needs its own bond, its own ivory record, and its own share of the bridge quota, which is where the cost multiplies. The ocean ledger enforces the limit at intake. A farm of 2000 identities would post 3188 proofs and burn roughly 82 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
